designDecisionsAndRationale: PCB geometry lives in semantic, in millimetres, in the KiCad board frame, rounded to 1 nm (roundNm); visual rounding of 0.01 would lose KiCad resolution (design 3.1, 13).
Page kind pcb is appended to PAGE_KINDS with no migration and no SCHEMA_VERSION bump, as for breadboard (design 3.1).
The PCB page has its own copper connectivity and ratsnest, not the lattice and target-netlist breadboard modules (design 5.5, 13).
Gerber and Excellon export reuses the packages/core/src/pcb writers with additive changes only, so breadboard ZIP bytes stay unchanged (design 7.2).
Pad anchor (footprintToBoard(fp, pad.at)) is the drill and snap point; copper is centred at padShapeCenter, which applies the drill offset (design 3.2, 6.4).
One core barrel line (pcb-board/index.ts with explicit named exports) is written by plan 09 alone in wave 3 so that wave-4 plans never edit packages/core (overview DAG).
intentionalTradeoffs: Silkscreen is not clipped against mask openings; the board designer owns silkscreen layout (design 13).
Text uses the Nodetto stroke font, so silkscreen text shapes differ from KiCad (design 13).
Vias are always tented; pad mask openings use a grown pad shape (design 13).
Zone fills are kept as read and never refilled, so edited copper may not match the fills (design 2).
The native CLI is an interpreter and is slow on large boards, as the Gerber import is (design 15).
supportedEdgeCases: KiCad 5 to 9 syntax differences: module/footprint, fp_text/property reference and value, quoted and bare atoms, net code or name, KiCad 5 centre/angle arcs vs start/mid/end, stroke width forms, fill forms, track arcs, user silkscreen layer names, tstamp/uuid (design 4.3).
Board-absolute pad and text angles minus footprint rotation, normalised to [0, 360); bottom-side footprints with pre-mirrored local geometry (design 4.3).
Pads with drill offsets (U1 pad 1 in the fixture), unknown pad shapes mapped to custom with a warning, zone polygons with arc entries kept as points with a warning (design 4.3, plan 09).

Rule-area zones and unsupported items (dimension, target, group, image, gr_bbox, gr_text_box, model) are skipped with one warning per kind; non-finite numbers drop the item with kicad.badNumber (design 4.2, 4.3).
A board with no outline is reported in the pcb gerber command; --strict writes nothing when warnings exist (plan 10).
Case-insensitive .kicad_pcb detection checked before the KiCad schematic/netlist and Gerber path checks (plan 13).
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Footprint flip to the other side, creating nets, paste and fabrication-layer Gerbers, inner-layer Gerbers, pick-and-place, SVG/PNG export of PCB pages, MCP tools (design 2).
Proving the angle, KiCad 5 arc sign and bottom-side conventions against real KiCad output; only self-authored fixtures are used (design 15).
Persisting layer visibility (user QA Q1) and a 45-degree track constraint (user QA Q5).
constraints: Follow AGENTS.md: English only, no emojis, cargo with CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true, strict TypeScript, bun run typecheck after TS changes, cargo fmt after Rust changes.
KiCad source is reference only; only self-authored fixtures; never commit third-party boards.
No regex split and no quadratic parsing (Boa native CLI); base names via lastIndexOf.

Workers follow impl-plans/active/kicad-pcb-00-overview.md 'Per-worker protocol' (sha256 before and after edits, intent snapshot, edit only writePaths and own progress log, no state-changing git, no workspace-wide formatter, foreground commands, no pipe into tee or head, sibling typecheck failures recorded and rerun, never counted as a pass).
Plans 10-13 run in parallel with disjoint writePaths; none edits packages/core.
residualRisks: KiCad angle convention, KiCad 5 arc sign and bottom-side drill offset are unproven against KiCad (design 15).

Wave-4 transient failures: plan 11 runs 'bun test packages/ui-solid' while plan 12 edits ui-solid files; plans 10 and 13 may build cargo concurrently. Handled by overview protocol item 8 and serial reconciliation.
